claims.text: The initial refractory HEA feedstock may use the W-Mo-Ta-Nb-V alloy system.
The initial W-Mo-Ta-Nb-V refractory HEA is a standard single-phase BCC alloy.
Such feedstock is typically fabricated by casting or powder metallurgy.
Laser powder-bed additive manufacturing of equiatomic W-Mo-Ta-Nb-V is feasible when favorable process parameters are selected.
Laser-based AM can build lattice or graded structures directly from the refractory HEA powder feedstock.
The AM intervention can preserve the alloy composition without substantial additional alloying.
The proposed benefit should persist at approximately 1200 °C or above under cyclic loading and extended dwell times.
AM produces microstructural refinement in the lattice beams and nodes.
AM architectural control improves the load-bearing topology of the component.
The proposed AM process reduces defect density.
Topological lattice design reduces effective component density.
Localized solidification and microstructural refinement during AM enhance high-temperature strength and creep resistance.
The refined AM microstructure preserves room-temperature ductility and toughness.
The lattice-structured AM component will improve high-temperature yield strength by approximately 10% or more relative to a conventionally processed component of the same composition.
The lattice-structured component will reduce effective density by several percent.
The lattice-structured component will retain room-temperature mechanical performance comparable to the conventional baseline.
Conventionally cast or hot-isostatically pressed baseline components have homogeneous, coarser microstructures and higher overall density.
Successful additive manufacture of the refractory alloy requires favorable and precisely controlled process parameters.
Long-term microstructural stability and oxidation resistance at elevated temperature remain unverified.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires an approximately 10% or greater strength improvement, but the falsification rule permits merely equivalent high-temperature strength, so a result below the predicted improvement could still be treated as supporting the hypothesis.
